maria: Heads-up: during last deploy we saw warmers spike cost by ~2.3x for a node pool. Any idea if keying entropy caused extra KV misses?
jordan: I saw that. Profiling shows 58% of warmers generated unique prefix keys due to user_id salt in prompt template. Cache hit-rate dropped from 72% to 21%.

jordan: Example offending template:
```
Welcome back, {{user_id}}! Here's your summary for {{date}}
```

alex: We should normalize keys: strip personal tokens and deterministic fields, then hash. E.g.:
```
def normalize_prefix(prompt):
  p = strip_user_fields(prompt)
  p = collapse_whitespace(p)
  return sha1(p)[:16]
```

devon: Also batching issue: warmers were single-request per key which killed batch occupancy. If we group warmers by normalized key we get larger batches -> ~30% lower p99 and 18% less GPU time.
kevin: Autoscale events made it worse. On scale-up we run warmers targeted at new hosts without global cache sync, causing duplicate KV fetches and extra load.
sre-bot: Created alert INC-2026: warmers-cost-surge and linked runbook :rotating_light:

jordan: Experiment proposal: scheduled 'light' prefill that seeds only top-10 keys per route, plus a low-rate synthetic dribble for long-tail keys during first 2h post-deploy. Estimates: +0.4% tokens/day => +12% overall cache hit-rate on average.
maria: Can you paste the perf table from the canary?
jordan: Sure (canary vs baseline):
```
metric           | baseline | canary
cache_hit_rate   | 72%      | 84%
p50_latency_ms   | 18       | 16
p95_latency_ms   | 120      | 95
token_cost($/day) | 1200     | 1254
```
alex: Note kernel interaction: after switching to optimized quantized kernel the small-batch deserialization path got ~2ms slower; preferring fp16 kernel for warmers improves throughput because warmers are latency sensitive and generate many small requests.
devon: Action items:
- implement key normalization in warmers
- change warmers to batch by normalized-key group
- schedule top-10 daily preseed per route
- run synthetic dribble for 2h post-deploy at 5 req/s/node
- add metric warmers.synthetic_hits and dashboard

maria: sgtm. I'll own rollout to 10% canary; will watch warmers.synthetic_hits, cache_hit_rate, and deployment_cost delta :thumbsup:
kevin: Also add rate limiter on synthetic dribble to avoid autoscaler feedback loops :eyes:
alex: Opening PR now with normalization + microbench results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
maria: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow after the PR lands.
